statement: In Ramadan of year 2 a large Quraysh caravan under Abu Sufyan was returning from Syria; the Emigrants' property in Makkah had been seized by Quraysh.
Ka'b ibn Malik: he went out seeking the caravan of Quraysh until Allah brought them and their enemy together without appointment.
Abu Sufyan diverted the caravan to the coast and sent to Makkah for help; an army marched out.
He consulted his Companions; a leader of the Ansar said that if he ordered them to plunge into the sea they would.
notes: Sahih Muslim (Anas): the speaker is named Sa'd ibn Ubadah; the Seerah works name Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. The script says 'one of their leaders'. Number from memory; not machine-checked.

statement: Ibn Mas'ud on al-Miqdad's words ('we will not say as the people of Musa said... we will fight on your right and left, before and behind you'), and the Prophet's face shining with pleasure.
The armies met at the wells of Badr, south-west of Madinah.
Al-Bara: the fighters of Badr numbered the same as Talut's companions who crossed the river, a little over 310.

Umar: on the day of Badr the idolaters were a thousand and his Companions 319; he faced the qiblah with hands outstretched and prayed 'fulfil what You promised me... if this band is destroyed You will not be worshipped on earth' until his cloak fell; Abu Bakr replaced it and said his pleading was enough.
notes: Direct speech. Content checked in the Muslim dataset (no. 4588), which explicitly says 'the day on which the Battle of Badr was fought', and Bukhari 3953. Abd al-Baqi number remains unverified.

statement: The Muslims had two horses and seventy camels.
Qur'an 8:11.
Qur'an 8:9 was revealed.
The battle was on 17 Ramadan, year 2.
Al-Bara: seventy of the idolaters were killed and seventy captured at Badr.
Abu Jahl was among the dead.
Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Bilal's former master, was killed at Badr.
notes: Machine-checked for his death at Badr at Bilal's instigation; that he had been Bilal's master is from the Seerah.

statement: Fourteen Muslims were killed.
Qur'an 3:123.
He instructed good treatment of the captives; some captives reported being given bread while their captors ate dates.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq (report of Abu Aziz ibn Umayr).

statement: Most captives were ransomed; some literate captives without means were freed in return for teaching children of the Ansar.
notes: Musnad Ahmad 2216 (Ibn Abbas), graded hasan by al-Arna'ut, from memory; not machine-checked. The debate over the captives and Qur'an 8:67 is left out; reviewer to decide whether it should be included.

statement: Of a veteran of Badr who erred he said: perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said 'do as you wish, I have forgiven you'.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the occasion (Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah); the quoted words are in the remainder of the narration, from memory.
